newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus tax rise proposed to aid defence spending.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus tax rise proposed to aid defence spending.

text.p: The Cyprus government submitted legislation to parliament on Thursday for a one percentage point increase in a tax on income to fund defence spending.

The rise aims at covering projected losses to the islands' defence fund after the government agreed to suspend payments by petroleum importers into the account last July and to ease implementation of a new defence programme.

Legislation tabled by the finance ministry sought an increase in defence taxation on gross income to three from two percent. It also sought a rise in tax to four from three percent on corporate profits, dividend income and interest earnings.
With the projected increase, it hopes to raise 123.8 million pounds ($267 million) in tax in 1997 over a forecast income of 89 million pounds in 1996.

In July the government suspended a special levy local petroleum importers were paying direct into the defence fund. The importers had complained they were losing money due to controlled retail prices and soaring oil prices.

The government opted for a suspension of the special levy to the defence fund rather than approve an increase in retail fuel prices, reviewed twice a year. The fund thereby lost an estimated 17 million pounds when the special levy was slashed.

The bill will have to be approved by the parliamentary finance committee and defence committee before it becomes law. The finance ministry has set January 1, 1997 as a target date for the legislation to be enacted.

Cyprus has engaged in a comprehensive programme to upgrade its defence capabilities for the past decade, with defence analysts estimating 1995 defence expenditure at three percent of gross domestic product with a peak of 7.4 percent in 1993.
The island's northern third has been occupied by 30,000 Turkish troops since 1974, when Turkey invaded in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military junta ruling Greece.
Defence fund contributions have been compulsory in Cyprus since 1984. The initial tax was 0.5 percent on gross income.
